content:
maya: quick sync — ran a mixed synthetic + replay bench this morning to isolate kernel selection + KV priming effects on autoscale. short notes below, pinging @aj for the kernel hints, @tim for autoscale metrics

bench-bot: run summary:
- harness: replay-based (mixed traffic) + synthetic tail spikes
- model: redwood-7b-v1 (fp16 -> int8 path tested)
- kernels: auto-selector vs hint=optimal_small_batch
- kv priming: none / prefix-only / full-kv-prime
- duration: 30m baseline + 10m spike
- endpoints: dedicated-pool-02 (8xA10G)

aj: nice. can you paste the exact bench commands?

maya: sure, these are what I used:

```
# replay harness
./bench/replay_run --trace=customer-traffic-2026-03-01.json --duration=1800 --concurrency=200 --kv-prime=prefix-only --kernel=auto

# synthetic spike
./bench/synth_load --pattern=poisson --p95=1200ms --duration=600 --concurrency=600 --kernel=hint:optimal_small_batch
```

maya: quick raw numbers (median of 3 runs):
- auto kernel + no-kv-prime: coldstarts=4, avg-scale-up=52s, p95-latency=420ms, kv-hit=8%
- auto kernel + full-kv-prime: coldstarts=1, avg-scale-up=18s, p95-latency=210ms, kv-hit=72%
- hint kernel + full-kv-prime: coldstarts=0, avg-scale-up=12s, p95-latency=180ms, kv-hit=74%

tim: whoa, the KV priming delta is huge on scale-up time. do we have per-GPU kernel selection logs to see if auto chose a slower kernel during onramp?

bench-bot: kernel-selection log excerpt (auto path during one ramp):
```
[00:00:03] kernel_selector: selected=kern_v2_mixed_batch heuristic_score=0.43 reason=batch_entropy_high
[00:00:10] kernel_selector: fallback=kern_v1_smallseq heuristic_score=0.38 reason=kv_cache_miss
```

aj: looks like auto is sensitive to early KV miss noise and picks a mixed_batch kernel that prioritizes throughput but has higher per-token latency for short sequences. That matches the p95 jump.

sophia: can we repro apples-to-apples? I want to see same sequence length distro and identical batching windows.

maya: done one pass — I fixed seq_len=64 for synthetic and forced batching=16ms across both runs. results:
- auto kernel + seq64 + full-prime: p95=190ms, avg-scale-up=16s
- hint kernel + seq64 + full-prime: p95=175ms, avg-scale-up=11s

eli: so kernel hint still edges out, but priming closes >60% of the gap. implies we should prioritize KV priming during canary rollout to cut coldstarts.

tim: agree. also worth noting dedicated pools with burst credits behave differently — did you run on dedicated with burst disabled?

maya: yes, two modes: burst-enabled (default) vs burst-disabled. numbers (auto kernel + full-prime):
- burst-enabled: effective-available-instant=+2 replicas for 90s (burst credit spent), avg-scale-up=14s
- burst-disabled: no instant burst, avg-scale-up=27s

aj: clarifying question: are we measuring scale-up as time until proxy returns 200 with tokens under p99 threshold, or time until instance registers healthy in control-plane?

maya: measured end-to-end (proxy starts returning non-503 + p95 tokens < 500ms). control-plane health registers ~6–8s earlier usually.

ops-bot: note added to incident log: "KV priming applied to canary group reduces cold-starts and scale-up latency."

sophia: methodology note for the doc: to make apples-to-apples we should fix these variables: sequence length distribution, batching latency window, request priority, and kernel hinting policy. also capture kernel selection trace and KV hit timeline.

aj: action items:
- aj: prototype a lightweight kernel-hint policy that forces small_batch for first 45s of ramp (helps latency), then toggles to mixed for throughput. test in shadow for 48h.
- maya: add automated KV priming step to replay harness (prefix prime then full prime option). version and add to bench configs.
- tim: gather metrics across 3 dedicated pools (2xA100, 8xA10G, 4xH100) for cost vs latency tradeoffs.
- sophia: write the apples-to-apples checklist and bench playback config.

eli: small consideration — forcing kernel hints might affect cost (small_batch uses more GPUs per token). include token-cost delta in experiments.

maya: noted. quick follow-up: should we default to enabling KV priming for new dedicated deployments until we get better auto-selector heuristics?

aj: tentatively yes for Dedicated-only. For Hosted, need to test customer impact.

tim: I'll scope a 2-week experiment: canary dedicated pool with kv-prime + 45s small_batch hint window. will report back next Wed.

maya: thanks all — I'll push the bench configs and logs to /bench/runs/1962504321/ and open a short PR with the checklist. :thumbsup:

bench-bot: artifacts uploaded: /bench/runs/1962504321/summary.json, kernel_traces.tar.gz, kv_priming_logs.tar.gz

aj: thanks — moving to follow-up channel: #eng-runtime-bench-results
